bullets.text: Apron Relief Program returned ~$1B to personal auto customers via 20% April and May premium credits; paused cancellations and non-renewals; gave $8M to charities and $1,000 to 2,000+ repair shops.

Personal auto profitability was strong through January, February, and pre-COVID March; significant accident declines followed restrictions, though true claims loss costs remain uncertain once normal repair practices resume.
Personal auto PIF +10% YOY; total PL PIF +8%; post-COVID auto new business applications dropped 23% on >20% decline in quotes, down from pre-COVID growth of ~9% in new apps.
PL NPW +8% YOY (+11% through February); Property NPW +15% to $403M; reduced in-force TNC NPW by ~$110.5M in March due to dramatic drops in miles driven.

Snapshot data showed post-COVID vehicle miles driven fell roughly one-third from pre-COVID levels, with regional variance across states; significant declines occurred in personal auto accidents as driving decreased.
Total portfolio return (0.60)%; issued $500M 10-year senior notes (3.20%) and $500M 30-year senior notes (3.95%) to fortify balance sheet; temporarily suspended open market common share repurchases.

Post-COVID Agency new applications dropped close to 30% as independent agency offices closed; Direct new applications declined 20%; made >$40M available to independent agents via 2020 Personal Lines bonus advances.

Transitioned most of nearly 43,000 employees to remote work; paid early portion of annual bonus in April; funded $2M Employee Relief Fund; covered employee COVID-19 medical treatment and telemedicine co-pays.

Pre-COVID commercial auto new applications rose 13% YOY, pacing toward a third consecutive record year, then plunged 29% post-restrictions (and ~35% by mid-April); maintaining Atlas, BOP, and Fleet investments.
Acquired 100% of ARX Holding Corp. on April 1, 2020, a year earlier than planned; believes the transaction will benefit efforts to expand reach and grow bundled auto and home Robinsons customers.
